original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Decide all nonzero-label rank counting cuts from odd-order cyclic characters of the actual generated paid-frame lattice, without a character-order cutoff.
scope_change_reason: The live mixed-target handoff already has rational, parity and ternary screens. Replace repeated modulus-specific exclusions by one complete finite odd-character screening implication, rather than repeating a scalar census or claiming a new register mechanism.
bottleneck_link: This pre-search audit can reject every order and arbitrary restored dirty workspace for one paid multiset before scalar synthesis. Passing it establishes only necessary cuts; a full formal word and native consumer bill are still missing.
stop_rule: Stop after the written finite-coverage proof, bounded exact CLI, independent character oracles and failure controls. No scalar-word search or construction expansion.
evidence: PROOF.md, RESULT.json, 784 direct-character cases, 476 finite-quotient density cases, 144 independent determinant cases, eight behavioral groups and four actual implementation mutants. Commands are registered in VERIFY.json.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance with derivation, implementation and checks. Review scope is author-checked; no independent human or proof-kernel review is claimed.
family_expansion_decision: Narrow to complete pre-search coverage. No physical or scalar construction expansion. Complete native, consumer, restoration, hosting, precision and recursive costs remain unknown, not zero.
optimistic_full_cost_budget: No supplier proposal or exponent improvement. The observable gain is completeness over all odd character orders, including composite orders missed by every prime-order test.

freshness.compatibility: Archive intake advanced main. AGENTS.md, autoresearch.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, catalogue, priority log, selected result, all proof inputs and applicable replay controls are unchanged. Preserve the initial scientific/provenance base; the new-directory patch applies to refreshed main without overlapping edits.
freshness.overlap: Final refresh reports complete pagination for 237 open PRs, 2413 closed/merged PR bodies and 1656 Discussion records. The exact-topic matches are this package and its own claim. Metadata search does not cover every diff or establish novelty.

validation.environment: Linux x86_64; CPython 3.12.15 for registered replay and CPython 3.13.5 for optimized direct replay.
validation.diagnostic_scope: Repository Ruff rules and extended correctness rules are clean. An exploratory ALL scan also reports incompatible docstring styles, annotation/docstring/line-length preferences, pytest conversions of Unittest assertions, intentional CLI prints and fixed-target subprocess style. These are not adopted as a new package standard or silently suppressed; the checker retains optimization-safe Unittest assertions, its explicit CLI and bounded local subprocess controls.

limitations: Written completeness proof, not proof-assistant formalization.
Only odd-order scalar characters; no complete dyadic, matrix-valued, native or physical test.
Rejection emits exact subgroup and target subsets with positive rational avoidance density, not an explicit root character or order bound.
No full selected or predecessor cold replay, supplier adoption or kappa change.

open_questions.question: Can one unequal-class eight-call dimension-three candidate pass rational, determinant, required dyadic and all odd-character screens before scalar synthesis?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Necessary pre-search coverage is now finite on the odd-character side, but no successful full formal word or complete supplier bill follows.
open_questions.first_step: Pin the actual frames and targets, run the complete odd-character CLI and existing rational, determinant and dyadic screens, and retain exact outputs before proposing a scalar search.
open_questions.blocked_by: A concrete candidate and a favorable complete native consumer budget are missing. Passing necessary screens alone does not justify family expansion.
